label: 《教父2》古铜暗调
style_en: Give the photo deep, readable near-neutral blacks, amber-brown midtones and warm ivory highlights. Concentrate warm color in existing yellow, brown and amber tones and gently mute cool hues. Keep midtone contrast firm and roll off highlights smoothly.

sources.note: Gordon Willis recalls a consistent yellow color structure and describes handling the period shift in Part II.
The interview discusses the warm yellow and orange look of Part II and Willis's control of the overall palette.

sources.note: Vittorio Storaro’s Painting with Light describes red, orange and yellow as successive colors in the early imperial palette. The rest of the film uses additional palettes.

sources.note: Janusz Kamiński describes the deliberately somber black-and-white cinematography. The study uses the main monochrome palette and omits selective-color scenes.

style_en: Use a cool, nearly monochromatic steel-blue grade with restrained saturation. Carry slate blue through the shadows and cooler midtones, ease warm hues toward muted neutrals, keep highlights closer to cool white, and use a firm but smooth tone curve.

label: 《飞行家》复古双色
style_en: Use a restrained two-color film palette. Preserve and enrich existing warm reds and oranges, shift existing blues and greens toward soft blue-green cyan, and compress the saturation of violet and pure blue. Use warm neutral highlights and a smooth highlight shoulder.

sources.note: Linus Sandgren identifies cyan, pink and blue as the romantic night palette, with amber as a different strand.

style_en: Use a deep but readable black point and keep dense lower midtones. Give existing amber, rust and olive hues more weight, with saturated warm highlights only where a warm color already exists. Keep near-neutral shadows dark and retain highlight texture.

sources.note: Vittorio Storaro discusses saturated colors, silhouetted darks and the importance of black. The warm-hue emphasis is a color-only adaptation of the warm highlights described in the article.

sources.note: Roger Deakins describes the orange and pink lens-filter combination for the Las Vegas exteriors and the resulting reddish look. Atmospheric smoke, lighting and set effects are outside this grade.

sources.note: DI colorist Eric Whipp describes lowering exposure and developing a stylized blue grade on the day-for-night material. The prompt carries over only the global tonal and color components.
